items.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I remember the first time I saw Janet Lynn skate in a skating show.

ctx.x: Do you have hobbies now that provide some part away from music for you?

Um, yeah, interests. Some interests. I mean now I’ve gotten all excited about astronomy again. I want to buy a telescope. I’m interested in Chi Gong and some kind of martial arts kinds of things. You know I like to read, I like to ride bikes, for years I loved dance, I love to go see dance. I’d like to take Flamenco dancing. I haven’t done it, but I’d like to. It’s just a matter of being in town enough to do it. Because I love Flamenco music. And that’s another thing that’s maybe going to be the result of having…

doing other things in life, and then suddenly you become so busy doing your music you aren’t paying attention so much to the other things in your life because they aren’t as important as the music. But what feeds the music? Music is fed by a deep and rich life. So I think it’s really important to have other things in your life that you can do with equal love.
